description: Control voltages taken from a point travelling round one of four polar equations, drawn on the screen with the point marked in red

params.text: Each press moves to the next speed multiplier and the lamp colour shows which — magenta 0.5x, cyan 1x, yellow 2x — though the rate changes by the square of that figure, so 0.5x quarters it
Moves to the previous of the four equations, wrapping from the first round to the last; the equation in force is printed across the top of the screen
Moves to the next of the four equations, wrapping from the last round to the first; the equation in force is printed across the top of the screen
Sets how fast the point travels round the equation; it is ignored entirely while anything is patched to the jack beside it
Sets the first constant of the equation, 0 to 10 in steps of 0.5; the value in force is printed into the equation across the top of the screen
Sets the second constant of the equation, 0 to 10 in steps of 0.5; the value in force is printed into the equation across the top of the screen

inputs.text: Takes over from the speed knob: 0V leaves the point almost stationary, and higher voltages send it backwards round the equation, fastest at 10V

outputs.text: The radius of the point in polar coordinates, ±10V
The horizontal position of the point, its radius times the sine of the angle, ±10V
The vertical position of the point, its radius times the cosine of the angle, ±10V

notes: patching anything into the speed jack cuts the speed knob out altogether; the knob is read only while that jack is empty.
the point never comes to rest: a small fixed amount is added to the angle every sample whatever the speed setting.
the screen is a display and not a control; nothing drawn on it responds to a click or a drag.
there is no reset or sync input, so nothing in the patch can return the point to the start of the equation.

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the speed knob; a negative voltage does nothing here.
